kurz: Let mushrooms give up their water first, then brown them in fat and salt at the end.
bild_im_kopf: Like puddles after rain: they have to evaporate before the ground warms up.
was_passiert: In the hot pan, water and juice come out first. Once this juice boils away, the temperature rises and the [[w-pilze|mushrooms]] brown. Too many mushrooms at once cool the pan, and they stew in their own juice.
warum_wichtig: The difference between grey, rubbery mushrooms and golden, savoury ones lies only in space, heat and patience.
faustregeln: For brown mushrooms: salt only once they have browned, otherwise they draw water.
schritte: Rinse or wipe the mushrooms briefly and pat them dry well.
Fry in a single layer in a large pan over high heat, in two batches if needed.
Do not stir constantly: turn only once the underside is brown.
Add butter, garlic, herbs and salt at the end.

mythos.behauptung: Never wash mushrooms, they soak up water.
mythos.richtig: Hardly true. Rinsed briefly, they take up very little water. What matters is patting them dry afterwards.
